notes: Furthermore, this account explains the odd phonological distribution of Sakha as in Section 2.1. Consider again the allomorphs -(n)Ill-, found before vowels, and -(n)IllI-, found before [-alveolar] consonants. The second /l/ in the geminate cluster cannot underlyingly be an /n/, because the regular assimilatory outcome of /-ln-/ clusters is [-nn-].
